references.text: Both verses address the requirement that sacrificial animals must be without defect to be acceptable to the Lord.
Continues the theme that sacrifices must be without blemish to be accepted by the Lord.
Parallel text regarding physical defects that disqualify, here applied to priests who may not approach to offer sacrifices.
Reiterates the prohibition against offering animals with defects to the Lord, as it is an abomination.
Prohibits castrated men from entering the assembly of the Lord, reflecting the principle of physical wholeness.
The fundamental requirement that a burnt offering must be a male without defect from the herd.
Peace offerings must also be without defect, whether male or female.
Malachi rebukes the people for offering blind, lame, and sick animals, which violates the principle of unblemished sacrifices.
